cards.name: Calligraphic
cards.summary: Artistic Media mode that draws a freehand stroke as if made with a flat calligraphy nib: the line is thick where you move across the nib angle and thin where you move along it. The result is a closed, fill-colored shape bound to an editable control path (an artistic media group), not a plain outline.
use_for: hand-lettered headline and signature strokes with thick-thin contrast
brush-script logo marks and monograms
decorative flourishes and swashes on invitations and certificates
ink-style line illustration
avoid: coloring it through the outline: the stroke is a filled shape, so set the fill color
mouse drawing that needs smooth curves: raise Freehand smoothing, or draw the path with the Pen / Bezier tools and give it a calligraphic outline instead
a nib effect that must stay editable as a simple stroke attribute: use an outline with a calligraphic nib (Outline Pen, F12: stretch + angle)
files going to apps that need plain vector shapes: break the artistic media apart (Object > Break Apart) and delete the control path before export
cards.how: Pick the Artistic Media tool (I) with a document open, then click Calligraphic on the property bar. Set Freehand smoothing, Stroke width (the widest the nib gets) and the calligraphic (nib) angle, then drag on the page. Direction relative to the nib angle decides the width, so test a curve before lettering. Afterwards select the stroke to change width / angle on the property bar, or reshape the control path with the Shape tool (F10).
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "6a38bf24-8983-42ce-9885-8d47a3fb2234" activates the Artistic Media tool (the harvest read the Artistic Media tool back from the data source); Application.ActiveTool then reads 117, a value outside cdrTools that Sprayer also lands on. The property bar mode was not read back, so check that Calligraphic is selected before drawing. Drawing the stroke is a hand gesture and the harvest records no call that creates a calligraphic artistic media stroke. Scripted substitute for the look: give a curve a calligraphic outline with Shape.Outline.NibStretch and Shape.Outline.NibAngle (a live outline, not an artistic media group).

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem was claimed to switch into Calligraphic mode; the batch only shows the data source reading back the parent Artistic Media tool (ActiveTool 117, shared with Sprayer), so the card now says the mode itself was not read back

cards.name: Expression
cards.summary: Artistic Media mode built for pen tablets: stroke width follows stylus pressure (and tilt / bearing when those inputs are switched on), so one drag gives a naturally swelling and tapering line. The result is a fill-colored closed shape bound to an editable control path.
use_for: sketchy hand-drawn illustration and inking with a stylus
organic hand-lettering with natural pressure taper
expressive line art for editorial, packaging or children's book illustration
avoid: mouse-only setups: a mouse sends no pressure, so the variation this mode exists for is lost; use Calligraphic or Preset, or shape widths with the Variable Outline tool (V)
precise technical or geometric lines: use the Pen / Bezier tools with a plain outline
coloring via the outline: the stroke is a filled shape, set the fill color
exports to apps that need simple vectors: break the artistic media apart first
cards.how: Pick the Artistic Media tool (I), click Expression on the property bar, set Stroke width (the width at full pressure) and Freehand smoothing, and switch on the stylus inputs you want (pressure, tilt, bearing) on the property bar; then draw with the pen. Press harder for a thicker line. Reshape the control path later with the Shape tool (F10) or change the width on the property bar.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "e8aed305-07ed-4af6-a4ba-a285bb7b7146" activates the Artistic Media tool (the harvest read the Artistic Media tool back from the data source); Application.ActiveTool then reads 103 (cdrToolDrawNaturalPen), the same value as Artistic Media, Preset and Vector Brush, so neither that read-back nor setting ActiveTool = 103 confirms Expression mode. The property bar mode was not read back, so check that Expression is selected before drawing. A script has no stylus and the harvest records no call that creates an expression stroke. Scripted substitute: a variable-width outline built with Shape.Outline.VariableWidthNodes.Add(t, Width) at positions t from 0 to 1 along the curve.

review.changes: script_api: same correction as the other modes; InvokeItem is proven to activate Artistic Media, not to select Expression (ActiveTool 103 shared with Artistic Media, Preset, Vector Brush)

cards.name: Preset
cards.summary: Artistic Media mode that wraps a drawn or selected path in a ready-made stroke shape from the preset list (tapered, swelling, pointed or blunt ends), giving a smooth brush-like line of a set width. The stroke is a fill-colored closed shape linked to its control path, so reshaping the path reshapes the stroke.
use_for: tapered swooshes and underlines under headlines
hand-drawn-look outlines for icons and spot illustrations
decorative dividers and swashes in print layouts
turning an existing curve into a tapered stroke
avoid: coloring via the outline: the stroke is a filled shape, set the fill color
textured or artwork-based strokes: use Vector Brush; objects scattered along a path: use Sprayer
precise width at chosen points: use the Variable Outline tool (V)
exports to apps that need plain shapes: break the artistic media apart first
cards.how: Pick the Artistic Media tool (I), click Preset on the property bar, choose a stroke from the preset stroke list, set Stroke width and Freehand smoothing, then drag on the page. To convert an existing path, select it and pick a preset stroke: the path becomes the control path. Reshape with the Shape tool (F10); recolor with the fill color.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "aebd9625-5777-42df-b266-c1a56f50c550" activates the Artistic Media tool (the harvest read the Artistic Media tool back from the data source); Application.ActiveTool then reads 103 (cdrToolDrawNaturalPen), shared with Artistic Media, Vector Brush and Expression. The property bar mode was not read back, so check that Preset is selected before drawing. The harvest records no call that applies a preset stroke. Scripted substitute for a tapered line: Shape.Outline.VariableWidthNodes.Add(t, Width) with a small width near t = 0 and t = 1 and the full width mid-path.

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem now described as activating Artistic Media with the mode not read back (was: switches to Preset mode)

cards.name: Sprayer
cards.summary: Artistic Media mode that sprays copies of objects from a spraylist (leaves, stars, candy, splashes ...) along the path you draw or select, with adjustable object size, dabs and spacing, spray order, rotation and offset. The result is a group of objects tied to the control path; reshape the path and the spray follows.
use_for: confetti, stars or leaves trailing along a curve on posters and greeting cards
decorative borders and garlands
quick foliage, grass or texture along a line in illustrations
repeat elements following a path on packaging
avoid: long paths with dense settings: object count and redraw time balloon; raise spacing or lower dabs
editing one sprayed object: break the artistic media apart and ungroup first
an exact, evenly spaced repeat of one object: use the Blend tool on a path
a single stretched stroke rather than separate objects: use Vector Brush
cards.how: Pick the Artistic Media tool (I), click Sprayer on the property bar, choose a category and spraylist, then drag on the page. Property bar options that matter: size of the sprayed objects (with incremental scaling), dabs per step and spacing, spray order (random, sequential or by direction), rotation (relative to the path or the page, with optional increments) and offset from the path. Select a path first and pick a spraylist to spray along it. To spray your own artwork, select it and save it as a new spraylist with the property bar's Save artistic media stroke button.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "caf8cf4f-6d6c-4789-8350-ab4f76a565cd" activates the Artistic Media tool (the harvest read the Artistic Media tool back from the data source); Application.ActiveTool then reads 117 (not a cdrTools member), the same as Calligraphic. The property bar mode was not read back, so check that Sprayer is selected before drawing. The harvest records no call that sprays along a path. Scripted substitute: walk the path with SubPath.GetPointAt / SubPath.GetTangentAt and place copies with Shape.Duplicate, rotated to the tangent (static copies with no live link to the path).

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem now described as activating Artistic Media with the mode not read back; how: replaced 'the spraylist settings add your own objects' (Spraylist options only pick images already in the spraylist) with saving your artwork as a new spraylist via Save artistic media stroke

cards.name: Vector Brush
cards.summary: Artistic Media mode (called Brush in older versions; not the pixel-based Painterly Brush tool) that stretches a vector brush stroke from the brush library (artistic, calligraphic, splash, scroll, object strokes ...) along the drawn or selected path. The artwork bends with the path and stays editable through its control path.
use_for: painted-look underlines and brush swashes behind headlines
textured hand-made borders and frames
illustration strokes with ink-splash or dry-brush character
a custom brand brush: save your own artwork as a stroke and reuse it along any path
avoid: tight curves with long or detailed brushes: the artwork kinks and distorts; smooth the path or pick a simpler stroke
true raster paint texture: use the Painterly Brush tool (J)
multi-colored library strokes keep their own colors; break the artistic media apart to recolor parts
exports to apps that need plain shapes: break the artistic media apart first
cards.how: Pick the Artistic Media tool (I), click Vector Brush on the property bar, choose a category and a brush stroke, set Stroke width and Freehand smoothing, then drag. Select an existing path first and pick a stroke to apply it to that path. The property bar's browse and save buttons load a stroke file or save the selected artwork as a new brush stroke.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "f7db3861-fa7d-4323-ae93-8903eb267ffe" activates the Artistic Media tool (the harvest read the Artistic Media tool back from the data source); Application.ActiveTool then reads 103 (cdrToolDrawNaturalPen), shared with Artistic Media, Preset and Expression. The property bar mode was not read back, so check that Vector Brush is selected before drawing. The harvest records no call that applies a library brush stroke. Closest scripted substitute: bend brush artwork along a path with Curve.CreateCurveMappedToStroke(Stroke, ScaleY, SelfWeld), where Stroke is the SubPath to follow (or CreateCurveMappedToStrokeAndReferenceLine), and place it with Layer.CreateCurve (a static shape, no live link).

review.changes: script_api: InvokeItem now described as activating Artistic Media with the mode not read back; named Stroke as the SubPath to follow in CreateCurveMappedToStroke

cards.name: 1-Leg Callout
cards.summary: Callout tool variant that draws a label with a single straight leader, from the point you are labelling to where the text sits, then takes your typed text. It makes a live callout object (leader, ending style, gap and optional halo behind the text) rather than loose lines and text. Not on the default toolbox: only 2-Leg Callout sits there (Dimension flyout); this one lives on the CalloutTool flyout bar.
use_for: product feature labels pointing straight at a detail
technical illustration and diagram annotations
infographic and map labels
packaging and dieline notes
avoid: leaders that must bend around artwork: use 2-Leg Callout (toolbox Dimension flyout) or 3-Leg Callout
speech bubbles and decorative callout shapes: use the Common Shapes tool
measured distances that must update with the object: use the Dimension tools (Parallel Dimension, Horizontal or Vertical Dimension)
cards.how: Add it through toolbox customization (its CalloutTool flyout also holds 2-Leg, 3-Leg and Callout) or select it by script. Press at the spot you want to label, drag to where the text should sit, release and type the label (gesture inferred from the variant name, not probed). Leader outline, arrowhead, ending style and gap are set on the property bar; the callout presets restyle a callout in one click.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "34bc1f24-e3df-40f7-995d-15133e220d4f" activates the tool (harvest: AppOrViewDataSource.ActiveTool reads back this GUID; Application.ActiveTool reads -1, so there is no cdrTools value for it). Placing a callout is a click-drag gesture. A script can restyle existing callouts through CalloutToolLib's CalloutShape (Gap, Ending, HaloVisible, HaloOpacity, HaloWidth, HaloJustification, LeaderCurve, TextShape). Creating one from script would go through Layer.CreateCustomShape(TypeID, Parameters): CalloutShape.TypeID reads the TypeID off an existing callout, but the TypeID value and the Parameters layout are not harvested; the safe substitute is a leader from Layer.CreateLineSegment plus a text object.

review.changes: how: flagged the press-drag gesture as inferred, not probed, and dropped 'text formatting' from the property bar list; script_api: noted CalloutShape.TypeID can read the TypeID off an existing callout

cards.name: 3-Leg Callout
cards.summary: Callout tool variant whose leader has three segments, so the line can step around other artwork before reaching the label; you place the leader points, then type the text. Like the other variants it makes a live callout object (leader, ending style, gap, halo). Not on the default toolbox: it lives on the CalloutTool flyout bar.
use_for: labels that must route around a dense illustration or exploded view
callouts running out to a column of labels in a margin
technical documentation with dog-leg leaders
avoid: simple straight labels: 1-Leg Callout is quicker; one bend: 2-Leg Callout
speech bubbles and decorative callout shapes: use the Common Shapes tool
measured distances: use the Dimension tools
cards.how: Add it through toolbox customization (CalloutTool flyout) or select it by script. Start at the point being labelled, place the two bends, finish where the text should sit, then type the label. The click sequence is inferred from the 2-Leg workflow and the variant name, not probed: try it on a scratch document first. Style the leader, ending and gap from the property bar or apply a callout preset.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "c53ca24d-d4c2-4cfa-b0cb-521015c1683b" activates the tool (AppOrViewDataSource.ActiveTool reads back this GUID; Application.ActiveTool reads -1). Placing the leader is hand input. Existing callouts can be restyled through CalloutToolLib's CalloutShape (Gap, Ending, Halo* properties, LeaderCurve, TextShape). Creation by Layer.CreateCustomShape(TypeID, Parameters) is unproven because the TypeID value and Parameters layout are not harvested (CalloutShape.TypeID can read the TypeID off an existing callout); the safe substitute is a polyline leader built with Layer.CreateCurve plus a text object.

review.changes: script_api: noted CalloutShape.TypeID can read the TypeID off an existing callout

cards.name: Callout
cards.summary: Fourth variant on the CalloutTool flyout, captioned just 'Callout'. It shares one tool state with the 1-, 2- and 3-Leg variants, so it is the same callout tool and makes a callout object, but the harvest does not show how it differs from them. CorelDRAW's UI config has a 'legless callout' state that switches off the gap and the leader arrowhead, so this may be the variant that places a label with no leader legs; treat its behaviour as unverified. Not on the default toolbox.
use_for: annotation labels on diagrams and technical illustrations
infographic and product labels when the fixed-leg variants do not fit
avoid: when the leg count matters: use 1-Leg Callout, 2-Leg Callout or 3-Leg Callout, whose behaviour follows their names
speech bubbles and decorative callout shapes: use the Common Shapes tool
live measurements: use the Dimension tools
cards.how: Add it through toolbox customization (CalloutTool flyout) or select it by script, then click the point or object being labelled and type the label. Whether it lays down a leader, and how many points it takes, was not probed: try it on a scratch document before relying on it. Style it from the property bar or with a callout preset.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "a4aa56b9-7975-48ba-987a-9427b478ff54" activates the tool (AppOrViewDataSource.ActiveTool reads back this GUID; Application.ActiveTool reads -1). Drawing the callout is hand input. Existing callouts can be restyled through CalloutToolLib's CalloutShape (Gap, Ending, Halo* properties, LeaderCurve, TextShape); creating one through Layer.CreateCustomShape(TypeID, Parameters) is unproven (TypeID value and Parameters layout not harvested; CalloutShape.TypeID reads it off an existing callout), so build a leader plus text from primitives instead.

review.changes: summary/how: removed the unfounded guess 'a free number of leader points' and the assumption that it draws a leader; now cites the UI config's legless-callout state as a possible reading, still unverified; script_api: TypeID note
